narrative.summary: Eswatini has no published AI-specific law, strategy or guidance. Its only AI-relevant national instrument is the Data Protection Act 2022, which regulates automated decisions and profiling and is enforced by the Eswatini Communications Commission (ESCCOM), also the communications regulator. A national AI strategy announced by the Ministry of ICT for 2024/25, a 4IR strategy and planned AI legislation have not been published.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Information, Communications and Technology
narrative.review_notes: Not yet verified from the official text: the national AI strategy, the 4IR strategy, the planned AI legislation and the Digitalisation Strategy 2024-2028. Official sources checked on 12 and 18 October 2026 include the communications and data protection regulator, the central bank, the procurement regulator and the standards authority; the government portal (including ministry pages and gazette listings) and the parliament website are still to be checked.

instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament of Eswatini (enacted by the King and Parliament of Eswatini)
instruments.current_status: Published in the Extraordinary Government Gazette Vol. LX No. 41 of 4 March 2022 as Act No. 5 of 2022; under section 1(2) it came into operation on publication in the Gazette. Section 55 gave existing processors two years (extendable to three by ministerial notice) to comply. The Act is administered by the Eswatini Communications Commission. No AI-specific law or AI guidance from the Commission was found on 2026-10-12.
instruments.summary: Eswatini's data protection law governing the collection, processing, disclosure and protection of personal data by controllers and processors established in, or using automated or non-automated means in, Eswatini. It designates the Eswatini Communications Commission as the supervisory authority with sanctioning powers, sets processing conditions and data subject rights, and covers biometric data as sensitive information. Section 45 restricts decisions with legal or significant effects based solely on automated processing intended to profile a person's personality or habits, subject to contract, legal-code and safeguard exceptions (including the right to make representations).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only national law found with a provision directly relevant to AI: the section 45 restriction on solely automated decision-making and profiling.

organizations.name: Eswatini Communications Commission
organizations.ai_governance_role: Communications regulator (ESCCOM) and the data protection authority under the Data Protection Act, 2022, which it administers and enforces (including the section 45 automated decision-making rule); publishes the Act and other ICT legislation. No AI-specific guidance found.

No official draft or adopted text found on 2026-10-12; gov.sz (Ministry of ICT pages) could not be reached (curl connection reset; WebFetch HTTP 503). Record once an official text is published. Update 2026-10-18: no official text found; the government portal (Ministry of ICT pages) and Parliament site still could not be reached, and the communications regulator's and central bank's site searches return no AI document.
